radioSource: ESP32-C3-MINI-1 & MINI-1U datasheet v2.2 (2026-05-06): Bluetooth LE transmit 170 mA peak at 0 dBm and receive 86 mA (Table 6-5); Wi-Fi transmit up to 350 mA (802.11b at 20.5 dBm, Table 6-4); external supply at least 0.5 A (Table 6-2), 3.3 V, 25 °C
notes: 4 MB on-module flash; it holds the firmware and the reading history (NVS or a LittleFS partition), so no external memory part is needed (datasheet v2.2, ESP32-C3-MINI-1-N4). Its USB Serial/JTAG controller on GPIO18 (USB_D-) and GPIO19 (USB_D+) programs the flash over USB, so flashing over USB-C needs no USB-UART bridge (datasheet v2.2, section 5.2.1.5 and the pin table). It runs from a 3.0–3.6 V supply (datasheet v2.2, recommended operating conditions). Its chip's current (ESP32-C3 Series Datasheet v2.4, 3.3 V, 25 °C): CPU running at 160 MHz with the radio off 23–28 mA (Table 5-8); radio receiving 84 mA and Wi-Fi transmitting up to 335 mA peak (Table 5-7, 100% duty); deep sleep 5 µA (Table 5-9). The chip datasheet gives no Bluetooth LE current figure; the module datasheet v2.2 does (bleTxMa, bleRxMa). Its strapping pins are GPIO2, GPIO8 and GPIO9 (datasheet v2.4, section 3.1): GPIO9 low when reset is released selects download boot (USB-Serial-JTAG or UART); GPIO0, GPIO1 and GPIO3 to GPIO5 are not strapping pins. Download boot also needs GPIO8 high at reset (Technical Reference Manual v1.4, Table 7.2-1: GPIO9 0 with GPIO8 0 is SPI download boot or, with GPIO2 0, an invalid combination); GPIO8 floats by default (datasheet v2.4, Table 3-1) and the module has no pull-up on it (module datasheet v2.2, Figure 8-1), so the board fits one (Espressif's peripheral schematic, Figure 9-1, R8 10k). GPIO2 only counts when GPIO8 and GPIO9 are both low; the datasheet still recommends a pull-up on it "due to glitches" without saying which
typical accuracy ±1.8 %RH and ±0.2 °C (SHT4x datasheet v1, Oct 2020, sections 2.1 and 2.2); I2C address 0x44; idle 80 nA
typical accuracy ±2 %RH and ±0.2 °C (SHTC3 datasheet v4, Dec 2022); I2C address 0x70; sleep 0.3 µA typ.

I2S digital MEMS microphone, 24-bit, bottom port: the sound hole goes through the PCB, so the case needs an opening under it (DS-000069 Rev 1.2, Aug 2016). Pins (Table 8): 1 WS, 2 LR, 3 GND, 4 SCK, 5 VDD, 6 SD. VDD 1.65 to 3.63 V, decoupled to GND with 0.1 uF; LR low puts its data in the left channel; SD needs a 100 kOhm pull-down (Table 8). Low-power mode at a 6.25 to 18.75 kHz sample rate draws 230 uA typ.; high-performance mode at 23 to 51.6 kHz 490 uA typ.; sleep (clock below 3.125 kHz) 12 uA typ. (Tables 1 to 3 and 5). TDK lists the part as end-of-life; check stock before a production run

maxMaSource: Diodes AP2112 datasheet DS39724 Rev. 2-2: output current 600 mA min
LCSC C5446 and Arrow listings (200 mA max); Torex's own datasheet not checked
Richtek RT9080 datasheet DS9080-09 (Dec 2024): 600 mA output for VIN at least 2.3 V; current limit 610 mA min
notes: Low-Iq regulator rated for the ESP32-C3 module's 0.5 A (DS9080-09): quiescent 2 uA typ, 4 uA max; shutdown 0.1 uA typ. Dropout at 600 mA for VOUT of 3 V or more: 0.31 V typ, 0.53 V max (the max is used here). TSOT-23-5 (1 mm tall, SOT-23-5 land pattern): 1 VIN, 2 GND, 3 EN, 4 NC, 5 VOUT, the AP2112K's pin order. EN high to run (tie to VIN); at least 1 uF ceramic on VIN and VOUT. JLCPCB extended part. One LCSC page flagged it not recommended for new designs; Richtek revised the datasheet in Dec 2024 and its product page gives no status: check the lifecycle before a production run

batteryDrainSource: TP4054 datasheet, electrical characteristics, IBAT at VCC = 0 V
notes: Single-cell Li-ion linear charger, 4.2 V float (4.158 to 4.242 V; the -42 suffix is this voltage, not a current). Charge current is set by the PROG resistor to ground, about 1000 V / RPROG: 10 kOhm 100 mA, 5 kOhm 200 mA, 2 kOhm 500 mA (465 to 535 mA), 1.4 kOhm 600 mA, 500 mA max by programming; the board generator fits 4.7 kOhm, about 210 mA (0.4 C on a 500 mAh cell). The 40 mA in its datasheet is only the test current for the float-voltage row. Pins (SOT-23-5): 1 CHRG open drain, low while charging, high impedance when done; 2 GND; 3 BAT; 4 VCC 4.25 to 6.5 V with at least 1 uF; 5 PROG. Ends the charge at 1/10 of the set current. With USB unplugged it draws 6 uA typ, 10 uA max from the battery (TP4054 datasheet, electrical characteristics, IBAT at VCC = 0 V).

JST SH 4-pin, 1 mm pitch, surface mount, right angle (the cable leaves along the board): the Qwiic / STEMMA QT connector. Pin 1 GND, 2 VCC (3.3 V), 3 and 4 the signals (I2C: SDA, SCL). A board-to-board link connector (docs/system.md); the cable is straight through.
